summary: Douglas Osto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Master's at the University of Washington and his PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. Around 2005, he became a Senior Lecturer at Massey University.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He completed his BA at James Madison University and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as Assistant Professor at East Tennessee State University (~2011–2014).
Dragana Majhen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, held posts there (attested 2002, 2020), and worked at the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.
Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who completed an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Dror Burstein is a Buddhist studies scholar who teaches literature at Tel Aviv University and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2014.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Reed College and Harvard University, he served as Assistant Professor at UC Irvine (~2002–2006) and held a post at UC Berkeley (~2006–2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).

Dungkar Lozang Trinlé (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gyuto Monastery. He was a full professor at Minzu University of China (~1960–1965), Director of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and taught at Tibet University (~1985–1997).
Durga Prasad Dikshit is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed doctoral studies under Baij Nath Puri and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

Durgamohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College, Vidyasagar College, and the University of Calcutta, where he also held an academic post.

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a D.Litt. under K. A. Subramania Iyer at the University of Lucknow and held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).
Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD at KU Leuven by 2018, where he also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology figure who studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. In 1990, he served as a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded and directed the Nitartha Institute (~1996) and directed the Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin.

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and the University of Vienna, where she earned a BA and completed an MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at institutions including the University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He held several posts at the Library of Congress (1968–1997) and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~1999–2010).
E. H. Johnston (1885–1942) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as a Professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1940).

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at King's College, the University of Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Paris (~1950–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).
